about: A player with this trait will more often look to drive forward with the ball down the left.
This makes a player more inclined to carry the ball forward on a run down the right.
Increases how often a player chooses to run with the ball through central areas.
A player with this trait makes more runs from deep to arrive in the opponent's penalty area.
A player who will make more attacking runs into the space between opposition full-backs and central defenders.
The player likes to get forward and join the attack.
The player favours the simple pass, shying away from through balls and longer distribution.
The player looks to thread through balls far more often.
A player who likes to attempt shots from outside the penalty area.
A player tends who to favour power over placement when shooting.
When shooting, the player leans towards accurate placement rather than sheer power.
The player curls the ball with more frequency and capability than average.
In one-on-one situations, the player likes to try to take the ball round the goalkeeper.

trait: Likes To Try To Beat Offside Trap
about: This player tends to frequently make runs in behind the opposition defence.
The player likes to get tight to mark when defending.
The player is more prone to showing dissent towards match officials.
They will look to hold the ball up in attacking areas.
The player drops off the line more often to collect possession in space.
They will play a simple pass-and-move action more often, giving and going while moving into space to receive in a better position.
When presented with a chance, the player is more likely to try to lift the ball over the goalkeeper.
The player is more likely to take command of midfield situations, using their attributes to set the team's tempo.
In attacking situations, the player is more likely to go for a spectacular overhead kick instead of a header, particularly when shooting.

trait: Looks For Pass Rather Than Attempting To Score
about: The player tends to lay a scoring chance off to a team-mate rather than take it on themselves.
This player tends not to attempt through balls and instead looks for safer options.
In possession, the player is more inclined to slow things down and weigh up their options.
They like to knock the ball past a defender and attempt to beat them for pace by racing on to it.
The player takes longer over their decisions when in possession.
As team-mates work into a crossing position, the player times late runs into the box.

trait: Tries To Play Way Out Of Trouble
about: Under pressure in a defensive position, the player favours passing or dribbling their way out over a safety-first clearance.
The player holds their position and makes no forward runs.
The player sticks to their preferred foot wherever they can, even when their weaker foot would suit the situation better.
The player is more willing to shoot directly from free kicks well outside the penalty area.
The player commits to a tackle more often. This is about how they engage, not simply about going to ground when challenging for the ball.
This player tends not to commit to tackles very often, with a focus on not engaging, rather than literally avoiding going to ground to win the ball.
Receiving the ball out wide, the player cuts inside to attack central areas more often.
The player keeps to the wide areas of the pitch whenever they can.
The player is more likely to strike free kicks with a lower, harder trajectory.

trait: Likes To Switch Ball To Wide Areas
about: The player more often switches the ball from the middle out wide with long, diagonal passes.
The player can launch a long throw with a low, flat trajectory much like a cross.
Given the choice, the player tends to run with the ball rather than pass it.
The player has little appetite for dribbling, moving with the ball less often than would normally be expected.

trait: Uses Long Throw To Start Counter Attacks
about: The goalkeeper likes to attempt to spring counter-attacks by throwing the ball out quickly from hand.
The player attempts shots from outside the penalty area less often.
The player does not like to make runs into the channels. For central players this means they prefer to stay in the middle, and for wide players they tend to hold a wide position.
On the ball at the left wing, the player more often cuts inside to attack through central areas.
With the ball at their feet on the right wing, the player is more likely to cut inside and attack central areas.
The player tends to cross from a deeper position rather than working a better opening higher up the pitch.
The defender is more likely to carry the ball forward into midfield positions.
The player tends to use the outside of their stronger foot rather than use their weaker one, even when their body position makes the weaker foot the more natural choice.

trait: Moves Ball To Right Foot Before Dribble Attempt
about: Before taking someone on, the player tends to shift the ball onto their right foot, adjusting their body shape to do so.

trait: Moves Ball To Left Foot Before Dribble Attempt
about: The player is more likely to set themselves on their left foot, adjusting their body shape before attempting a dribble.
The player shows for the ball and asks for it into feet rather than into space or in the air.
The player approaches play with more flair, bringing a wider range of skills into their game.
The player sets out to annoy and frustrate opponents, hoping to make them lose focus and their temper.
They enjoy beating an opponent more than once, dribbling past them then cutting back to do it all over again.
When the ball is out of play, the player looks to the crowd for a positive reaction.
The player tends to shoot first time rather than take a settling touch, except in a one-on-one, where they will pick whatever the situation calls for.
The player is more willing to attempt passes over longer distances.
The player pushes to take free kicks.
The player insists on taking penalties.
The goalkeeper is more inclined to play the ball with their feet.

trait: Play Football For As Long As Possible
about: The player looks to extend their career for as long as possible, dropping down the levels rather than retiring.
The player would rather retire while still at the top than carry on playing down the levels.
